restaurant.name: Hu's Noodle Nook
restaurant.description: A cozy, family-feel ramen and noodle shop in Edmonton's Oliver neighbourhood. Known for its house Tan Tan (peanut-sesame, spicy pork) ramen and udon, long-simmered tonkotsu broth, Hu's own Chinese-style noodle bowls, tempura, donburi and hot stone nabe.
restaurant.reservations: Call (780) 250-2600. Walk-ins welcome; most reviewers report no wait.
restaurant.hoursNote: Hours from the restaurant's Instagram bio; holiday hours may differ.
restaurant.pricePerPerson: CA$10–30 (most reviewers: $10–20 at lunch, $20–30 at dinner)
restaurant.parking: Free parking in the building's lot. You must register your licence plate on the tablet at the front counter (covers about 3 hours); the lot is monitored. Bicycle parking available.
restaurant.accessibility: Ground-floor restaurant in a residential tower. Confirm specific needs by phone.
restaurant.kids: Very kid-friendly: high chairs, kids' plastic plates and cutlery, change table in the washroom; staff are noted as great with children.
restaurant.groups: Best for 1–4 people; small dining room with counter and table seating. Call ahead for 5–8.
restaurant.noise: Quiet to moderate — reviewers repeatedly say it's easy to talk.
promotions: Online: free can of pop on orders of $50+.
Limited time: free 1 pc tempura shrimp with Hu's Classic Noodle, Red Flame Noodle and Tan Tan Udon.

loved: Tan Tan is the signature: rich, layered, slightly creamy peanut-sesame broth that people finish to the last drop.
Noodles cooked perfectly — chewy, not too soft or firm.
Service is the standout (4.85/5): warm, attentive, patient with first-timers, great with kids, helpful with vegetarian picks.
Cozy, clean, quiet little room — easy to talk; good for a solo lunch, a date or a family dinner.
Usually no wait; free parking (register your plate).
Big menu beyond ramen: udon, Hu's Chinese-style noodle bowls, tempura, donburi, hot stone nabe, izakaya snacks.
constructive: Bowls are right-sized — a regular bowl is plenty for most guests. Bigger appetite? Pair it with a small plate like karaage or gyoza, or a mini donburi.
Ramen purists sometimes find the plain tonkotsu lighter than 24-hour specialist shops; the flavoured broths (Tan Tan, Black Garlic, Spicy Garlic Miso) win more fans.
Specials like tsukemen can sell out.
